discovery: Discovery of the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune

nominees.name: David C. Jewitt
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

motivation: In 1992, after five years of patient, technically demanding CCD searches at Mauna Kea, Jewitt and Luu discovered 1992 QB1, the first object found in a vast population of icy bodies beyond Neptune. Their discovery showed that the outer solar system is not empty. It is a structured disk of primordial material, and it is the reservoir of short-period comets. This changed our physical picture of how planetary systems form and evolve. It explained Pluto's place, revealed the dynamical signature of giant-planet migration through resonant populations, and gave us a local analogue of the debris disks seen around other stars. The discovery opened a new environment to physical study, culminating in New Horizons' flyby of Arrokoth. It is a model of what a well-chosen, hard-won measurement can do: redirect a field and change what humanity knows about its own planetary neighbourhood.
